name: Fino Payments Bank Ltd
title: Fino Payments Bank Ltd - 543386 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 was weak: EBITDA fell to INR 43.1 crores from INR 56 crores in Q4 FY26 after the UPI P2M B2B pause, with throughput down 10% year-on-year and no B2B relaunch before Q4 FY27.

triggers.quote: the total throughput declined by 10%, largely due to the strategic recalibration of our UPI P2M B2B business segment

triggers.label: EBITDA INR 56 cr to 43.1 cr

red_flags.quote: saw 13% sequential revenue decline as it continued to face industry headwinds

evasions.quote: we are actually waiting for some clarification on the amount where this will be...

summary.headline: Fino Payments Bank Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 43.1 crore from INR 56 crore in Q4 FY26, while net revenue margin hit a record 42.8% after the UPI P2M B2B pause.
summary.overview:
Management described Q1 FY27 as one of the toughest quarters in the bank's history, with the UPI P2M B2B business paused for recalibration and relaunch tentatively in Q4 FY27. Fee income was INR 234 crore and made up over 75% of revenue, while CASA's share of revenue rose from 45% to 54% QoQ. Referral loan disbursals rose to INR 628 crore (up 214% YoY). The bank reiterated its small finance bank (SFB) transition timeline, with the readiness submission to RBI targeted for end-Q4 FY27 and the RBI deadline of 5 June 2027. Throughput fell 10% YoY but rose 3% QoQ.</overview>

segments.name: B2B CMS
segments.commentary: Throughput grew 26% QoQ to INR 18,000 crore; revenue rose 5% QoQ, though the segment faces pricing pressure.

segments.name: Traditional transactions (remittance, micro ATM, AePS)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 13% QoQ as cash-to-UPI migration continued to weigh on the segment.

segments.name: UPI P2M B2B
segments.commentary: Paused for strategic recalibration; at least a couple of quarters to relaunch, tentatively Q4 FY27. UPI throughput grew 14% YoY to INR 60,000 crore.

segments.name: Liability franchise / CASA
segments.commentary: Average deposits grew 12% YoY to INR 2,772 crore; CASA share of revenue rose to 54% from 45% in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Referral lending
segments.commentary: Disbursals of INR 628 crore in Q1, focused on gold loan, affordable housing and loan against property.

guidance_outlook: SFB readiness submission to RBI by end-Q4 FY27; RBI's 18-month window ends 5 June 2027.
Senior management expected to join between September and October 2026; technology stack for the loan journey expected ready by Feb 2027.
SFB opex of about INR 10 crore expected in FY27 P&L, including hiring.
SFB target: 90% secured book, blended portfolio yield around 14%, NIM 8-9%, credit-deposit ratio around 70%, CASA around 65%.
Management said the FY30 business plan and the earlier 20%-plus ROE expectation are unchanged; the CEO said it is too early to guide on longer-term ROE and top-line growth.
Plan to open 40 new branches in year 1 of SFB operations.
capex_capacity: Finacle core banking went live in the prior quarter; Q1 focus shifted to stabilisation and Phase 2 (lending, new products).
Lending modules (LOS, LMS and other lending applications) being built with technology partners; PwC appointed for SFB readiness.
Technology investment is largely done; the first three SFB phases expected to complete after FY27.
Operating costs flat YoY despite inflation; continued investment in technology, risk management and AI.
demand_pricing: Total throughput fell 10% YoY but rose 3% QoQ; the decline reflects B2B UPI P2M recalibration, cash-to-UPI migration and a focus on higher-quality merchants.
Net revenue margin improvement is attributed to a shift toward the ownership-led business.
Newly acquired customers becoming UPI-active within the same quarter: 68%.
Management said it would be a definite positive for the bank if a proposed MDR on B2B transactions above INR 2,000 is implemented; quantification not given.

qa_highlights.question: What rates will the bank charge on gold, LAP and housing loans, and how will the SFB book be priced?
qa_highlights.answer: Referral loans are currently offered through partner NBFCs; post-SFB the bank aims to price better than them. The SFB book is planned at 90% secured with a blended yield of about 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the bank benefit from the proposed MDR changes?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chief Digital and Liabilities Officer said it would be a qualitative yes for the bank; the impact is still being modelled and will be recalibrated with the B2B UPI P2M relaunch.

qa_highlights.question: Would BPCL's stake in the holding company affect the bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the holding company and the listed OpCo are separate, the bank's capital is sufficient, and no holding-company investment activity affects the bank.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20%-plus ROE guidance hold, and what are the NIM and liability assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO confirmed the 20%-plus ROE guidance holds. The CEO cited liabilities of INR 2,800-3,000 crore, cost of funds 1.4%, current yields of 6-6.5%, and a target SFB NIM of 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SFB operational step-by-step plan and is there a non-compete on referral customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Senior hires are due September-October; technology partners are engaged; readiness is targeted for end-Q4. There is no non-compete, because referral customers are the bank's own customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BC business be sold and is a reverse merger required?
qa_highlights.answer: BC activity for other banks is prohibited for an SFB. The BC business needs a different approach, possibly restructuring, with a concrete plan expected in about a quarter. The HoldCo/OpCo structure is unchanged for now.

risks_watch: B2B UPI P2M relaunch timing (tentatively Q4 FY27) depends on the ecosystem and is uncertain.
CEO transition: a new CEO has not been named, and the Board and RBI are handling the process; the candidate is not yet disclosed.
BC business divestment or restructuring plan and its timing are still undefined.
SFB readiness submission by end-Q4 FY27 ahead of the 5 June 2027 deadline, with leadership hires due Sep-Oct and a lag expected before operations start.
Term deposit accretion in rural and low-income segments; management said term deposits will be used for stickiness, not aggressive sourcing.
Net revenue margin and fee-income quality versus the falling traditional transaction revenue and throughput.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on operations, confident on the SFB roadmap. Management acknowledged a tough quarter and gave no quantified guidance on the MDR impact, the BC divestment, or the new CEO. It was firm that the FY30 plan and the 20%-plus ROE view are unchanged.
